title: MemOS — where the paper and the code part ways
subtitle: Only the divergent steps are drawn. Each node states both sides; the lane says which stage of the pipeline the divergence sits in.
source: paper arXiv:2507.03724v4  ×  MemOS @ 8553242   ·   servers/memos/verification.md, 148 assertions checked (104 ✓ / 10 ✗ / 34 ◐ / 0 ?), §5 divergence table D1-D16
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · paper ↔ code divergence
legend_notes: The headline: MemOS's one named contribution — P-TRANSMUTE, migrating memory between plaintext/activation/parameter — has zero implementation. component_init.py hardcodes act_mem=None, para_mem=None; A6 INTERNALIZE is empty on the code side.

The second most concrete finding is structural: the paper's MemVault/vector-DB abstraction doesn't exist. Neo4jCommunityGraphDB pops every embedding out of the graph node and ships it to Qdrant — vectors never touch Neo4j.

A3 ADMIT is where the method degrades hardest: dedup/conflict/version/reorganize all exist as code but default OFF (is_reorganize=False), are unreachable (add_before_search, zero call sites), or need a field the wrapper never sends (merged_from).

The OS-metaphor naming (MemOperator/MemVault/MemStore/...) is not cosmetic — grepping the repo for any of the paper's class names returns zero hits; the real module boundaries are mem_reader/ mem_scheduler/ mem_cube/ graph_dbs/.
